identity: Neutral isocyanic acid H-N=C=O, CAS 75-13-8, singlet ground state and bent near-prolate asymmetric rotor. It is distinct from HOCN, HCNO, HONC, cyanate anion and condensed acid. JANAF C-053, NASA HNCO and exact ATcT gas identity agree; the appendix identity exclusion is resolved without changing the frozen 93-species screen.
recommendation: Prioritize a retained-thermal ATcT energy candidate for HNCO. The major discrepancy is an obsolete energy anchor; the available evidence does not require replacing the inherited thermal function at the same time.
science: The original JANAF evaluation, printed page 601, was visually inspected. Its 1970 energy selection combines older photodissociation and solution-derived arguments and gives Hf(0) about -98.7 kJ/mol. ATcT 1.228 instead gives -115.86 kJ/mol, supported by later threshold experiments and a thermochemical network. With consistent atoms, the physical atomization-energy increase is 17.260 kJ/mol, raising the retained-fit K by 3.99057 at 1500 K and 1.68030 at 4000 K. Current/JANAF is within 1.65% at the four nodes; energy-aligned JANAF/NASA differs by only 0.59-0.69%, isolating energy as the dominant issue.
modern: The NASA energy cites East 1993 and is already much closer to ATcT than JANAF. The 2004 focal-point abstract and 1996 threshold abstract support the direction of the later energy revision; they are not represented as independent confirmation of all ATcT inputs. The full 2021 author paper computes HNCO internal partition functions only through 500 K, using resolved rotational levels plus harmonic vibrations. That is useful convention evidence but does not establish a new 1500-4000 K thermal model.
importance: HNCO participates in nitrogen/carbon chemistry and is observed in molecular environments; its trace equilibrium inventory on this hot hydrogen-rich grid is separate from its potentially important kinetic and cooler-cloud roles.
conventions: JANAF explicitly uses ground-state weight one and symmetry number one. The 2021 partition values already set nuclear-spin degeneracy to one, so no second division or arbitrary electronic factor is allowed. A future state model must handle the quasilinear bending spectrum and natural-mass versus principal-isotope convention.
followup: Build the exact ATcT-minus-JANAF atomization-energy correction while retaining the current thermal shape and fitting residual; verify G/H/S/Cp, then perform fixed-network substitutions. Evaluate HNCO and NCO separately and together because their energy network and interconversion are coupled. Original 1996/2004 full texts are useful optional ancestry, not a prerequisite for this bounded source review.
